title: UniformlyConvexHolder.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Constrained minimization of a convex differentiable function f over a nonempty compact convex set C. The gradient is L-Lipschitz on C, with L>0. Strong convexity of f is not assumed.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A query Sum.inl x returns ∇f(x) for every x∈C, at every call index and every seed. There is no gradient error or stochastic noise assumption; responses must be exact.

oracle.label: linear_minimization
oracle.details: A query Sum.inr g returns an exact minimizer of ⟨g,x⟩ over C for every direction g, call index, and seed. Selection among minimizers may vary. Each gradient or linear-minimization query counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/UniformlyConvexHolder.lean: spec.admissible, Sum.inr clause; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: C has diameter at most D>0 and is uniformly convex with parameters a>0 and q>3: tx+(1−t)y+a t(1−t)‖x−y‖^q z∈C for x,y∈C, t∈[0,1], and ‖z‖≤1. A global Hölder error bound holds: for every x∈C there exists y∈argmin_C f with ‖x−y‖≤c(f(x)−f*)^(1/r), where c>0 and r>2. Public information consists of E, L, and a feasible x0; D,a,q,c,r,ε are not public algorithm inputs.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/UniformlyConvexHolder.lean: UniformlyConvexSet; Public; Params; spec.publicInput; spec.valid; spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output must belong to C and satisfy f(output)−f*≤ε, where ε>0 and f* is attained on C.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the ε objective-gap guarantee must hold almost surely under the output probability law, rather than merely in expectation.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This specializes smooth constrained convex optimization through the joint assumptions of power-type uniform convexity of the feasible set with q>3 and a global Hölder error bound with r>2. These geometric and growth restrictions distinguish it from the basic smooth convex benchmark. No proved results or budgets were supplied, so no rate comparison was performed.

descriptionHtml:
Frank–Wolfe with Uniformly Convex Constraints

We consider minimizing a convex function f:E→R over a compact uniformly convex set C in a finite-dimensional real inner-product space E, starting from a given x0∈C. The gradient is L-Lipschitz on C, with L>0, and distance to the minimizer set satisfies a Hölder error bound. The oracle returns ∇f(x) at x∈C or a minimizer of a queried linear functional over C. We analyze short-step Frank–Wolfe. For ε>0, the goal is a feasible output x¯ with f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely, where x⋆ minimizes f on C and the randomness comes from oracle tie-breaking.

The optimization problem is minx∈Cf(x). Write ⟨⋅,⋅⟩ for the inner product and ∥⋅∥ for its induced norm. The parameters satisfy L,D,a,c,ε>0,q>3,r>2. The algorithm receives only E, L, and x0; the parameters D,a,q,c,r,ε may enter only the oracle-call budget.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Uniformly convex feasible set). The set C is compact, contains x0, and satisfies ∥x−y∥≤D,x,y∈C. For every x,y∈C, t∈[0,1], and z∈E with ∥z∥≤1, tx+(1−t)y+at(1−t)∥x−y∥qz∈C.

Assumption 2 (Convexity and smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable at every point of C. For all x,y∈C and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y),∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Hölder error bound). There exists x⋆∈C minimizing f over C. For every x∈C, there exists a minimizer y∈C such that ∥x−y∥≤c(f(x)−f(x⋆))1/r.

There are two query types. The gradient oracle returns ∇f(x) at x∈C. A linear minimization query accepts any g∈E and returns an atom s∈C satisfying ⟨g,s⟩≤⟨g,x⟩,x∈C. Every reply must satisfy its stated condition; selection among minimizing atoms may depend on previous queries and oracle randomness. Both query types count toward a single total oracle-call budget.

Our result is algorithm-specific: we analyze short-step Frank–Wolfe initialized at the given point x0. Each iteration first queries the gradient and then a minimizing atom, and updates according to gk=∇f(xk),sk∈argmins∈C⟨gk,s⟩,γk=min{1,⟨gk,xk−sk⟩L∥sk−xk∥2},xk+1=xk+γk(sk−xk). When sk=xk, the quotient is defined to be zero, so γk=0. Each completed iteration uses two oracle calls. After a total budget of N≥0 calls, with N an integer, the output is the last completed iterate x¯=x⌊N/2⌋. If N is odd, the final gradient query leaves this output unchanged.

The required accuracy is x¯∈C,f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s., where P is the law of the oracle randomness.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.ProperSpace

open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace OracleTemplate.FrankWolfe

variable {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]

noncomputable def shortStep (L : ℝ) (x gradient atom : E) : E :=
  x + min 1 (⟪gradient, x - atom⟫ / (L * ‖atom - x‖ ^ 2)) • (atom - x)

noncomputable def shortStepFrankWolfe (L : ℝ) (x0 : E) : Algorithm (E ⊕ E) E E where
  State := Bool × E × E
  initial _ := (false, x0, 0)
  query state := (0, if state.1 then Sum.inr state.2.2 else Sum.inl state.2.1)
  update state reply :=
    if state.1 then (false, shortStep L state.2.1 state.2.2 reply, 0)
    else (true, state.2.1, reply)
  output state := state.2.1

end OracleTemplate.FrankWolfe

open Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.UniformlyConvexHolder

open OracleTemplate OracleTemplate.FrankWolfe

def UniformlyConvexSet {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (C : Set E) (a q : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ C, ∀ y ∈ C, ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ z : E, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 →
    t • x + (1 - t) • y + (a * t * (1 - t) * ‖x - y‖ ^ q) • z ∈ C

structure Public where
  E : Type u
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  L : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.innerE Public.finiteE

structure Params extends Public where
  D : ℝ
  a : ℝ
  q : ℝ
  c : ℝ
  r : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  f : p.E → ℝ
  C : Set p.E

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := p.E ⊕ p.E
  Reply p := p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 < p.D ∧ 0 < p.a ∧ 3 < p.q ∧ 0 < p.c ∧ 2 < p.r ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p I oracle :=
    IsCompact I.C ∧ UniformlyConvexSet I.C p.a p.q ∧ p.x0 ∈ I.C ∧
    (∀ x ∈ I.C, ∀ y ∈ I.C, ‖x - y‖ ≤ p.D) ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ I.C I.f ∧
    (∀ k seed x, x ∈ I.C → HasGradientAt I.f (oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inl x)) seed) x) ∧
    (∀ k seed x, x ∈ I.C → ∀ y ∈ I.C,
      ‖oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inl x)) seed - oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inl y)) seed‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∀ k seed g, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inr g)) seed ∈ I.C ∧
      ∀ x ∈ I.C, ⟪g, oracle.answer k (0, (Sum.inr g)) seed⟫ ≤ ⟪g, x⟫) ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.C, IsMinOn I.f I.C xstar ∧
      ∀ x ∈ I.C, ∃ y ∈ I.C, IsMinOn I.f I.C y ∧
        ‖x - y‖ ≤ p.c * (I.f x - I.f xstar) ^ (1 / p.r))
  successful p I output P :=
    ∃ xstar ∈ I.C, IsMinOn I.f I.C xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _),
        output ω ∈ I.C ∧ I.f (output ω) - I.f xstar ≤ p.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p A := A = shortStepFrankWolfe p.L p.x0

end LongTails.Setups.UniformlyConvexHolder
